data.title: Targa Resources raised to Buy at TD Cowen, seeing peer-leading EBITDA growth
data.description:
Targa Resources (TRGP) rises 3.3% in Friday's trading as TD Cowen upgraded the oil and gas infrastructure company to Buy from Hold with a $350 price target, raised from $275, citing expected Permian Basin wet gas growth and peer-leading EBITDA growth.

TD Cowen's Jason Gabelman said Targa (TRGP) has demonstrated an ability to grow its Permian gas processing volumes at a better pace than underlying robust Permian gas growth, which should continue with support by producer Permian activity and expanding gas-to-oil ratios.

Targa's (TRGP) outperformance is supported by its strong relationship with growing producer customers, Gabelman said, forecasting 17 new processing plants through 2030 and two plants per year beyond 2030, underpinned by maintaining market share plus its relationship with Permian-growth leader Exxon.

The analyst also sees Targa's (TRGP) free cash flow yield improving to greater than 10% in 2028 from 6% in 2026 compared to peer FCF yield at 8.5% in 2030, supported by EBITDA growth driven by new processing plants and completion of a large capital project in the Speedway NGL pipeline, which could cause the market to lean more towards a 2030 valuation methodology than 2027 EBITDA.

data.title: Advent, FedEx-led consortium clears threshold for InPost deal
data.description:
Private equity firm Advent International LP and FedEx (FDX)  cleared a threshold for acquiring Polish parcel-locker company inPost SA (INPOY) (INPOF) in a €7.8 billion ($9.3 billion) deal.

The consortium cleared the minimum acceptance threshold of at least 80% of shares tendered for its offer to purchase inPost, according to a Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited an emailed statement. About 89.1% of inPost shares were tendered.

The consortium announced the deal in February and said it would begin a public offer at €15.60 a share in cash.

data.title: AT&T extends contract with Dallas Cowboys
data.description:
AT&T (T) has extended its contract with the Dallas Cowboys to power AT&T Stadium's mobile network and fan connectivity.

The company will also debut new stadium technology during the 2026 season to include fan experiences, mixed reality, and AI-powered moments.

AT&T Stadium will now be equipped with AT&T Turbo to give every fan, including customers of other carriers, high-priority network access to post and stream during the game and Starbase Connection, which transforms fan-submitted photos into custom Cowboys hype videos across stadium boards.

Fans can also “Pose with the Pros” using augmented reality, and put themselves in mixed reality catch-and-compete moments with the players.

The partnership keeps AT&T’s name on the stadium. 

AT&T Stadium currently boasts one of the largest networks in the U.S. with more than 261 miles of fiber and close to 1,000 antennas throughout the stadium.   

AT&T (T) has been a corporate sponsor of the Dallas Cowboys since 1996 and obtained stadium naming rights in 2013.
